blocks.title: Why Tracing with OpenTelemetry and OpenLLMetry matters here

spans.text: Problem statement: An LLM workflow needs traces that connect web requests, model calls, retrievers, and tools. The learner's job is not to memorize Tracing with OpenTelemetry and OpenLLMetry; it is to decide what to build or change, what evidence the system may use, and how to tell whether the change improved percentage of incidents with end-to-end trace coverage.

Running case: OpenTelemetry span plan for LLM and retrieval operations. We will keep this same case through the lesson so each idea has a job: frame the problem, explain the mechanism, choose a design, test the implementation, and decide what to do next.

Before reading on, predict: if model calls are visible but disconnected from the request that triggered them, where would you look first - the input, the state or data, the model boundary, the validation check, or the release process?
The lesson skips definition-drilling and spends its effort on edge cases: state boundaries, hidden coupling, observability gaps, and the evidence that would change a production decision.

items.text: Product framing: Tracing with OpenTelemetry and OpenLLMetry matters when it changes a user-visible decision, release gate, or operational workflow.
Engineering framing: Tracing with OpenTelemetry and OpenLLMetry matters when it changes data, state, prompts, model behavior, tools, schemas, traces, or runtime constraints.
Validation framing: the lesson is not complete until the team can measure percentage of incidents with end-to-end trace coverage on examples that resemble the real workload.

blocks.title: Core workflow: the mechanism in the running case

spans.text: Core workflow opens the machinery behind Tracing with OpenTelemetry and OpenLLMetry. In the running case, the important question is: what exactly changes between the user's request and the final output?
Mechanism means turning subjective quality into repeatable cases, assertions, rubrics, and release gates.
Two framings for the same idea

items.text: Plain framing: imagine a reviewer following a checklist. They need to see what came in, what was considered, what was rejected, and why the final answer is safe to use.
Technical framing: imagine a trace. It should expose inputs, state, external evidence, model or algorithm output, validation result, and owner for exceptions.

blocks.title: Case study: what changed after the first review

spans.text: The first prototype works on the demo path. Then a reviewer runs the uncomfortable case: model calls are visible but disconnected from the request that triggered them. The output still looks confident, which is exactly why the lesson needs a richer artifact.

The team does not restart from scratch. It adds one missing control to OpenTelemetry span plan for LLM and retrieval operations: a stricter input contract, better source metadata, a validation assertion, a human-review edge, a rollback trigger, or an audit log depending on where the failure appeared.

items.text: Decision made: keep the thin slice, but block release until the failure is observable and repeatable.
Evidence added: the artifact now shows the input, intermediate evidence, final output, and pass/fail reason.
Metric promoted: percentage of incidents with end-to-end trace coverage becomes part of the release gate instead of a dashboard someone checks later.

spans.text: Case-study takeaway: a useful Tracing with OpenTelemetry and OpenLLMetry design makes the wrong answer inspectable before it reaches users.

blocks.title: How this breaks in practice

spans.text: The failure mode to keep in view is concrete: model calls are visible but disconnected from the request that triggered them. Use it as a diagnostic lens while reading every design choice.

items.text: Golden cases are too easy and miss the failures users actually report.
An assertion checks wording but not the required behavior or source.
The release gate averages away a serious failure in a high-risk slice.
The broad warning sign: percentage of incidents with end-to-end trace coverage gets worse even though the final answer or artifact still looks polished.

spans.text: Debugging rule: inspect the earliest place where bad evidence can enter and the latest place where validation should have stopped it.

blocks.avoidWhen: Avoid advanced optimization while the team still cannot reproduce or detect: model calls are visible but disconnected from the request that triggered them.
blocks.ruleOfThumb: Make the failure visible before making the system more sophisticated.

capstone.prompt: Create a one-page release-ready plan for OpenTelemetry span plan for LLM and retrieval operations. Include: the user problem, realistic input, mechanism, design choice, runnable or reviewable check, metric (percentage of incidents with end-to-end trace coverage), failure case (model calls are visible but disconnected from the request that triggered them), owner, and the next rung after this lesson.
